newsitem.title: CHINA: ATHLETICS-MA DEFENDS HIMSELF AGAINST ACCUSATIONS OF STEALING.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-MA DEFENDS HIMSELF AGAINST ACCUSATIONS OF STEALING.

text.p: Chinese track coach Ma Junren, whose women runners shattered three world records in 1993, has defended himself against accusations of stealing athletes' prizes saying he was entitled to half their winnings.

The coach said he had an agreement signed by five directors of China's State Physical Culture and Sports Commission promising him 50 percent of all winnings at the World Championships in Stuttgart in 1993, the Beijing Youth Daily reported on Wednesday.
The Commission refused on Thursday to comment on any agreement with Ma over the distribution of prizes while Ma could not be contacted for comment.
Long distance runners Wang Junxia, Qu Yunxia and Liu Dong were each awarded a new Mercedes-Benz car for winning gold medals in Stuttgart but never received their prizes.

Ma's team of runners, dubbed "Ma's Family Army", broke up in 1994 after double world champion Wang Junxia led a mutiny in protest against training methods and accusing the coach of pocketing athletes' prizes.

The newspaper said Ma kept one of the $30,000 cars for himself and handed over the others to the Sports Commission in northeastern Liaoning province where his training camp is based after his athletes walked out.
It said he now planned to give two of the cars and cash to the runners.
Within a month of his team's collapse Ma crashed one of the cars, putting himself and his wife in hospital with serious injuries.
Wang Junxia went on to win the 5,000 metre gold medal at last year's Atlanta Olympics while none of Ma's new army of women athletes qualified for the Olympic team.
